title: Polymicrobial Wound Infection from Cat Bite
patient: Adult with infected cat bite wound, 3-day delay, fever, green discharge, foul odor
diagnosis: Polymicrobial Wound Infection (Pasteurella multocida, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Bacteroides fragilis, Streptococcus anginosus group)
hpi: Cat bite 3 days ago, presenting with worsening infection, fever, green discharge, foul-smelling wound on lower extremity

exam.relevant: Swelling, erythema, green foul-smelling discharge at bite site

missed.why: Gram stain gives immediate Gram+ vs Gram- and morphology data while culture is pending
Rule out retained tooth fragments, foreign bodies, subcutaneous gas (NF), baseline bone assessment. Osteomyelitis changes lag 10-21 days behind infection.
Stray cat ran away. Cannot observe/test for rabies. HRIG provides immediate passive immunity while vaccine kicks in. Rabies is 100% fatal once symptomatic.
Standard post-exposure prophylaxis -- inactivated virus stimulates antibody production over 7-14 days. Given with HRIG for complete PEP.
Cat bites are tetanus-prone (puncture, animal saliva, high infection risk). Last booster >5 years ago requires update.

clinicalPearls.cat_bite: Think Pasteurella (always in cat saliva — 50-75% of cat bites)
clinicalPearls.delayed_presentation: 3-day delay allows secondary contamination (Pseudomonas from environment)
clinicalPearls.augmentin_resistance: Pseudomonas has intrinsic resistance: AmpC beta-lactamase (not inhibited by clavulanate) + low outer membrane permeability + efflux pumps

timing.note: 1 negative patient update before correct treatment
